headline: Every brand posts a positive comp as margins compress
summary_short: Williams-Sonoma's fiscal Q1 2026 (ended May 3, 2026) net revenues rose 4.4% y/y to $1,805M on a 4.8% comparable brand revenue gain with every brand positive, while operating margin slipped 60bps to 16.2% and diluted EPS grew 4.3% to $1.93.
summary_long: Net revenues rose 4.4% y/y to $1,805M on 4.8% comparable brand revenue growth, led by West Elm (+8.5%) and Williams Sonoma (+5.0%); every brand posted a positive comp. Gross margin fell 30bps to 44.0% on a 100bp merchandise-margin decline, partly offset by supply-chain efficiencies and occupancy leverage. SG&A rose 30bps of sales on higher employment and general expenses, pulling operating margin down 60bps to 16.2%. Net income was roughly flat at $231M; diluted EPS grew 4.3% to $1.93 on buybacks. Guidance reiterated: FY2026 revenue +2.7% to +6.7%, comps +2.0% to +6.0%, operating margin 17.5%-18.1%. Cash ended at $652M after $288M buybacks and $85M dividends; inventories rose 9.0% y/y, including ~$60M tariff costs.

drivers.explanation: Comparable brand revenue rose 4.8% with every brand positive: West Elm +8.5%, Williams Sonoma +5.0%, Pottery Barn Kids and Teen +4.5%, Pottery Barn +1.0%.
Gross margin fell 30bps as a 100bp merchandise-margin decline was partially offset by supply-chain efficiencies (+50bps) and occupancy leverage (+20bps); occupancy costs rose 3.0% y/y.

SG&A rate rose 30bps on higher employment expense (+30bps) and general expenses (+10bps), partly offset by advertising leverage (-10bps), pulling operating margin down 60bps despite the smaller gross-margin decline.
Net income held roughly flat as lower net interest income (-$2.6M) was largely offset by a lower effective tax rate (22.5% vs 23.0% a year ago), per the income statement.
Net margin fell to 12.8% from 13.4% because net income held flat while revenue grew 4.4%, arithmetic dilution from top-line growth outpacing profit growth.
Basic EPS grew 3.7% versus roughly flat net income because basic weighted-average shares fell about 3.8% y/y (123.1M to 118.4M) on continued buybacks.
Diluted EPS grew 4.3% versus roughly flat net income because diluted weighted-average shares fell about 4.0% y/y (124.8M to 119.9M) on continued buybacks.

CEO Laura Alber called it a "strong start," citing every brand's positive comp and continued outperformance despite housing-market cyclicality; the company reiterated fiscal 2026 and long-term guidance unchanged.
